questions.stem: What is the term for the total money owed to the bank at the end of the time period?
questions.solution: The term for the total money owed to the bank at the end of the time period is 'Amount'. This is because 'Amount' represents the sum of the principal and the interest. 'Principal' is the initial amount borrowed, 'Interest' is the extra money paid on top of the principal, and 'Rate of interest' is the percentage used to calculate the interest.

questions.stem: What is the total amount that Suvidya returned to the bank if she borrowed 30000 rupees at 8 p.c.p.a. for a year and had to pay back 2400 rupees over and above what she had borrowed?
questions.solution: The total amount Suvidya returned is the sum of the principal and the interest. The principal is 30000 rupees and the interest is 2400 rupees. So, 30000 + 2400 = 32400 rupees. questions.stem: If the principal is 50000 rupees and the rate of interest is 12 p.c.p.a., what is the interest for one year?
questions.solution: The interest for one year is calculated using the formula: (Principal × Rate of Interest) / 100. For 50000 rupees at 12 p.c.p.a., the interest is (50000 × 12) / 100 = 6000 rupees. '5000' is 10% of 50000, '7000' is 14% of 50000, and '8000' is 16% of 50000.

questions.stem: If the principal is 25000 rupees, time is 4 years, and the interest is 6000 rupees, what is the rate of interest?
questions.solution: The rate of interest can be calculated using the formula for simple interest, which is (Interest × 100) / (Principal × Time). Plugging in the values, (6000 × 100) / (25000 × 4) = 6%. The other options do not satisfy this calculation. 4% and 5% would result in lower interest amounts, while 7% would result in higher interest.
